title: Inject keystrokes into the caller window: find it, classify it, deliver by surface
desc: How the harness finds the window of the process that called it -- console, Windows Terminal, or a Chrome widget -- and pushes keystrokes such as a numeric answer plus backspace into it focuslessly. The three delivery surfaces already exist as separate skills; this recipe combines find, classify and per-surface send.
steps: WHY THIS RECIPE EXISTS: the pieces were all present but uncombined. A caller wanting to auto-answer a prompt that appears in its OWN window, such as an agy numeric permission menu, a console set-p, or a Chrome chat editor, needed to stitch three separate skills together. This records the join so nobody re-derives it. The shape is identical to the exec delivery-channel ladder: FIND the target, CLASSIFY it, then choose the SEND path by class. One transport can never cover all three surfaces, exactly as the input-delivery investigation proved for exec.

STEP 1, FIND THE CALLER WINDOW. Never use the foreground window as the caller signal because it drifts. Walk the ANCESTOR PROCESS CHAIN from the calling process up to the nearest ancestor that owns a usable window, and use that. Return Zero and skip if none exists. Full rules in standard-appbot-window-t1-core and its howto and ref tiers. The 3-tier validation cascade is wkfind-caller-hwnd-validation-3tier-pattern and the process-chain patterns are wkfind-quick-process-chain-caller-window-detection-patterns. The launcher already computes this for placement via CallerPlacementResolver, so the hwnd is usually already in hand.

STEP 2, CLASSIFY BY WINDOW CLASS, because the send path depends entirely on it. Call GetClassName on the resolved hwnd. CASCADIA_HOSTING_WINDOW_CLASS means Windows Terminal. A Chromium widget class such as Chrome_WidgetWin_1, or a hwnd known to be a CDP-driven tab, means a browser surface. A classic console such as ConsoleWindowClass or conhost is the third. Misclassifying here sends bytes to a surface that cannot receive them, the same silent no-delivery failure the exec input investigation spent days on.

STEP 3A, WINDOWS TERMINAL uses PostMessage WM_CHAR to the InputSite child, focusless and with no 10s UIA timeout. EnumChildWindows for the Windows.UI.Input.InputSite.WindowClass child, then PostMessage of WM_CHAR value 0x0102 with the character, one per keystroke with a small delay and NO SetForegroundWindow. This is TerminalWindowHelper TypeToTerminal, verified focusless by screenshot. A control character rides the same path: to push the digit 1 then a backspace, send WM_CHAR 0x31 then WM_CHAR 0x08. Full design in wt-terminal-a11y-type-read-design.

STEP 3B, CHROME WIDGET uses CDP Input dispatchKeyEvent after DOM focus on the target node, NOT a synthetic JS KeyboardEvent. ProseMirror and tiptap editors, which are the Claude chat surface, IGNORE a synthetic JS KeyboardEvent while dispatchEvent still returns true, so a naive pump believes it succeeded and the text just sits there. SendPromptFocuslessAsync focuses the node by CDP nodeId, bypassing Runtime evaluate and the focus-steal-guard, then dispatches real key events. Full mechanism and the auto-submit pump in cdp-prompt-pump-focusless-enter.

STEP 3C, CLASSIC CONSOLE is the gap. A conhost console reads via ReadConsoleInput from its input buffer, so neither a pipe write nor a WM_CHAR to the frame reliably lands. A real INPUT_RECORD via WriteConsoleInput on the console input handle is the correct primitive, and it is NOT yet wired as an a11y or exec send path. This is the same read-mode boundary the exec input-delivery investigation hit: raw-console readers need console input records, stream readers need a pipe, and a single mechanism serves neither universally. Cross wkexec-conpty-keystrokes-ladder-ref and verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static.

VERIFY DELIVERY BY PRESENCE, never by silence. After sending, confirm the TARGET changed: the prompt advanced, the character echoed, the menu selection moved, not merely that no error appeared. An absent error is exactly how a non-delivering send passes review, the lesson that cost most of the 2026-07-23 and 2026-07-24 exec investigation. For a terminal, a11y read via TextPattern DocumentRange GetText reads the surface back. For a Chrome widget, read the editor DOM. Assert the injected keystroke is actually there.

THE ACTUAL MOTIVATING CASE, and the point of the '1\b' sequence (user 2026-07-24) -- I initially over-generalised this into a three-surface transport recipe; the real goal is narrower and cleverer. agy keeps raising UNWANTED permission popups, and the harness wants to AUTO-SELECT option 1 the instant one appears, WITHOUT disturbing the user's live chat. The danger: the harness cannot always be 100 percent certain the focused surface is the permission popup versus the ordinary prompt/input box. So the injected sequence is not a bare '1' but '1' FOLLOWED BY A BACKSPACE. If the surface really is the numeric permission menu, the '1' selects option 1 and the trailing backspace is harmless (the menu already acted on the keypress). If the harness guessed wrong and the '1' landed in the user's PROMPT editor instead, the backspace immediately DELETES it, leaving no stray character in what the user was typing. So '1\b' is a SELF-CLEANING keystroke: correct when it hits the menu, self-erasing when it hits the wrong surface. This is why the sequence matters and why delivery must be focusless (never steal focus from the user's chat) and why verify-by-presence still applies -- confirm the popup actually dismissed, and confirm the prompt editor is unchanged afterwards. The per-surface send paths above are HOW to deliver it; this is WHY. Design note: prefer to answer only when classification is confident, and rely on the self-erasing tail as the safety net for the residual uncertainty, not as the primary mechanism.

PRECONDITION CHECK -- the popup must ACTUALLY APPEAR, and under exec-driven agy it does NOT. agy-sandbox-popup-extermination-bypass step 11 CONFIRMED that when agy.exe is driven through wkappbot exec's ConPTY, agy's own PreToolUse hook stdin read HANGS forever waiting for an EOF the ConPTY chain never delivers, so antigravity-cli hits its 30s hook timeout and treats it as fail-open ALLOW -- meaning the permission popup is never raised at all and every command runs unchecked. CONSEQUENCE for this recipe: the auto-select-1-plus-backspace defence is only meaningful for an agy session a HUMAN is running in a real terminal, where the popup genuinely appears and would otherwise interrupt the user's chat. It is NOT applicable to an exec-driven agy session, where there is no popup to answer (the deeper bug is that the harness is not enforcing at all, which is a security hole to fix, not a popup to dismiss). So before wiring auto-answer: (1) confirm the target is a human-run agy in its own terminal, not an exec child; (2) DETECT the popup is really present (its distinctive numeric-menu text on the surface) rather than firing on a timer; (3) only then send 1-backspace focuslessly. If the popup is absent, sending anything is pure risk with no benefit. This precondition is why detection must be presence-based, and it ties the recipe to the correct scenario instead of the one where the harness is silently disabled.

THE PRIMARY SOLUTION ALREADY EXISTS -- auto-answering the popup is a FALLBACK, not the fix. agy-harness-popup-deadlock-ref step 10 VERIFIED live 2026-07-23 that when the harness verdict channel is correctly wired, agy raises NO native approval prompt at all: the PreToolUse hook writes a contract-shaped decision, the agy screen prints Tool call denied by pre-tool hook, and no popup appears. So the intended zero-popup architecture is the harness BEING the gatekeeper (approvalMode plus a wired hook), which suppresses the prompt at the source -- NOT keystroking 1 into a prompt after it appears. Five defects had to be fixed for that channel to work (a null-Substring marker probe, the hook not reading args nested under toolCall.args.CommandLine, a Claude-style nested emit object agy rejects, a message field with the same effect, and a trap delegating to the wrong-dialect gemini sender) -- all now closed. THEREFORE the 1-backspace auto-answer belongs ONLY to the degraded case: the harness is not wired, or its hook crashed or timed out, and a real native prompt is sitting in front of a human, interrupting their chat. In that fallback the self-cleaning 1-backspace is the right minimal touch. But do NOT build it as the primary mechanism, and do NOT add it on top of a correctly wired harness where the popup will never fire -- that is dead code guarding a condition that a healthy install already prevents. DECISION ORDER: first confirm the harness verdict channel is wired and working (agy prints the hook denial, no popup); only if it is NOT, and a human is being interrupted by a live prompt, does the caller-window auto-answer earn its place. Cross: agy-harness-popup-deadlock-ref (the wired zero-popup proof), agy-sandbox-popup-extermination-bypass (the exec-driven fail-open case where no popup fires for the opposite reason).

OWNERSHIP 2026-07-24: the live agy wiring -- the PreToolUse verdict channel, the installer, the popup path, any real agy session work -- is the DOCS TEAM's charge, not this repo's ROOT. This skill is TECHNICAL ADVICE only: it records what mechanisms already exist (caller-window ancestor walk, focusless WM_CHAR and CDP dispatchKeyEvent send paths), what the 1-backspace self-cleaning keystroke is FOR and when it applies, and the two conditions where it does NOT (a correctly wired harness raises no popup at all, and an exec-driven agy fails the hook open so no popup fires either). A ROOT session here should knowledge-ify and advise up to this line and stop -- do not wire agy, do not edit its installer or hooks, do not run live agy sessions to test popup behaviour. Hand this recipe to whoever owns the agy surface and let them build against it. This mirrors the general rule that cross-repo live work belongs to the team that owns the surface (see the cross-repo edit convention).

THE cleaner PATH is exec --reply, not caller-window WM_CHAR (user 2026-07-24). When a target IS driven through wkappbot exec, the reactive responder built this session already does auto-answering without any of the find-window / classify / send-per-surface machinery in this skill: 'wkappbot exec <target> --reply "Requesting permission=>1" --reply-max 100' watches the child's own live output and injects 1 the moment the prompt text appears, all inside exec, focusless by construction. That is strictly nicer than resolving the caller hwnd and posting WM_CHAR, and it is the preferred route for any EXEC-DRIVEN child. TWO THINGS GATE IT TODAY, both recorded elsewhere in this cluster: (1) --reply is not finished -- a literal-pattern rule stalls the relay for a still-undiagnosed reason (wkexec-conpty-keystrokes-ladder-ref steps 10-13), PipeInput.cs line 79 does a blocking stdin write on the relay thread, and OnMatch.cs runs an untimed regex; these are the open work items for the reply feature. (2) exec-driven agy specifically fails its own PreToolUse hook OPEN (agy-sandbox-popup-extermination-bypass step 11), so under exec no agy permission prompt fires for --reply to match -- the prompt only exists for a HUMAN-run agy. SO THE DIVISION IS: for an exec-driven child that genuinely prompts, finish --reply and use it. For a human-run agy prompt interrupting a live chat, the caller-window 1-backspace fallback in this skill applies. And whenever the harness verdict channel is correctly wired, neither is needed because agy raises no prompt at all. Prefer, in order: wired harness (no popup), then exec --reply (auto-answer the child), then caller-window injection (last-resort for a human-facing prompt).
